assumptions: Capture reagents and particle counters have sufficient sensitivity and buffer compatibility after appropriate controls.
Sufficient conditioned-medium yield can be produced to run matrixed stability conditions across >=3 independent lots.
biological_rationale: MISEV2023 emphasizes that membrane-protection and orthogonal capture distinguish EV-associated signals from non-vesicular secretome co-isolates (ev-misev2023-quality-framework). Rodent intranasal studies demonstrate downstream sensitivity to material state (ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi, ev-kodali-2017-status-epilepticus) but do not define stability-linked attributes. Establishing stability-indicating intact-EV signals will enable linking preserved product identity to downstream functional assays and reduce risk from undetected membrane/cargo loss during storage or formulation.

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Qualitative co-localization of particle-count peaks with capture-positive fractions and loss of captured signal after detergent+protease treatment (pass/fail).
candidate_quality_attributes.name: EV identity and purity
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: Orthogonal capture co-localization and detergent/protease sensitivity to report preserved membrane-associated surface phenotype under storage/formulation conditions.
candidate_quality_attributes.uncertainty: Moderate: assay interference remains a risk until capture-compatibility and spike-in controls confirm validity.

edges.competing_explanation: Apparent signal loss could be assay interference from excipients or capture-reagent incompatibility rather than true membrane/cargo loss.
edges.missing_experiment: Matrixed stability and buffer-compatibility study pairing orthogonal identity/cargo analytics with controls for assay interference.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: consensus guidance supports that intact-EV metrics report membrane protection, and rodent data highlight processing sensitivity, but program-specific stability linkages are untested.

edges.competing_explanation: Even if stability-indicating metrics are found, in vivo delivery failures may persist due to route- or species-specific clearance independent of product stability.
edges.missing_experiment: Short-interval in vivo recovery studies using materials pass/fail by the proposed stability attributes.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate-to-high: large-animal delivery uncertainty increases the importance of identity/stability gates, but cross-species delivery barriers remain a competing cause of in vivo detectability failures.

nodes.statement: Orthogonal intact-EV analytical signatures (capture-positive surface-marker co-localized with particle peaks; detergent/protease-sensitive captured signal; protected-cargo fingerprint; particle:protein ratio) operationally report membrane integrity and EV-associated cargo protection in the drug substance.

Storage and formulation exposures (temperature, time, freeze-thaw cycles, excipient classes, device-shear) that damage EV membranes or strip associated cargo will abolish or substantially alter these orthogonal signatures while bulk particle counts may be preserved.

If orthogonal signatures change reproducibly with defined exposures, those signatures can serve as stability-indicating, qualitative gates for acceptable storage/formulation envelopes and comparability decisions to support downstream potency and bridging studies.

competing_explanations: Apparent attribute changes reflect capture-reagent incompatibility or assay artifacts rather than true EV membrane or cargo loss.
In vivo detectability failures may arise from administration route, species clearance, or labeling artifacts instead of stability-related loss.
dependencies: Establish capture-compatibility buffer panels and exogenous intact-EV spike-in controls prior to full matrix testing
Generate >=3 independent conditioned-medium lots from the selected source-cell bank/passage range
design_question: Which orthogonal intact-EV identity and protected-cargo signals (capture-positive surface-marker co-localized with particle peaks, detergent/protease-sensitive captured signal, protected-cargo fingerprint, and particle:protein ratio) are reproducibly lost or altered by clinically relevant storage and formulation exposures and therefore serve as stability-indicating attributes for SGL-001?
expected_measurable_effect: Defined orthogonal attributes will be qualitatively preserved under acceptable storage/formulation/device conditions and reproducibly lost (or substantially altered) under defined failure conditions (e.g., multiple freeze-thaw cycles, specific excipient classes, elevated temperature), enabling pass/fail gating for shelf-life and formulation compatibility.

experiment.assay: Orthogonal stability workflow: (1) fractionation (density or SEC) with particle counting per fraction; (2) immuno-capture on intact fractions and capture ELISA/bead readout for canonical surface markers; (3) detergent + protease/RNase protection testing on captured material; (4) protected-cargo profiling (targeted small-RNA panel ± detergent; targeted proteomics ± protease); (5) total protein and protein:particle ratio per fraction; (6) capture-compatibility panels to detect assay interference.
experiment.comparator: Within-lot paired comparisons: baseline no-exposure control versus matrixed conditions including defined storage temperatures/durations, 0/1/3 freeze-thaw cycles, and candidate formulation/device exposures. Include detergent/protease-disrupted aliquots and capture-compatibility buffer-only controls.
experiment.control: Negative controls: buffer-only and detergent-disrupted samples. Positive controls: characterized small EV preparation processed in parallel and spike-in synthetic standards for omic assays. Capture-compatibility controls for each formulation buffer.
dependencies: Analytical harmonization and capture-compatibility panels established before interpretation
Sufficient lot material to run matrixed condition testing
Access to targeted omics platforms with spike-in controls
experiment.failure_criterion: No reproducible, qualitative change in orthogonal intact-EV signatures across tested conditions (n >= 3 lots), or observed changes are explained by assay interference per compatibility controls.
experiment.falsification_outcome: If failure criterion is met, the hypothesis is falsified: these orthogonal intact-EV signatures are not stability-indicating for SGL-001 and the program should (A) not rely on them for stability/compatibility gates, (B) investigate assay limitations or alternative attributes (tighten fractionation, protected-cargo panel redesign), or (C) pursue secretome-centric product definitions.
experiment.hypothesis_tested: Orthogonal intact-EV analytical signatures (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks; detergent/protease-sensitive captured signal; protected-cargo fingerprint; particle:protein ratio) are reproducibly altered (lost or substantially changed) by unacceptable storage/formulation/device exposures and preserved under acceptable conditions, enabling use as stability-indicating attributes.
experiment.primary_readout: Qualitative preservation vs loss of co-localization of particle-count peaks with capture-positive fractions and loss of captured signal after detergent+protease/RNase compared with baseline control, per condition and lot.
experiment.question: Which orthogonal intact-EV identity and protected-cargo signals are reliably lost or altered by clinically relevant storage/formulation exposures and therefore serve as stability-indicating attributes for SGL-001?
required_material: MSC-conditioned medium from >=3 independent production lots (same source-cell bank/passage range)
Enriched small-EV preparation (program-defined bounded fraction) from each lot sufficient for matrixed testing
Candidate formulation excipient matrix (pH variants, ionic strength variants, representative non-ionic surfactant concentrations, sugar/polyol stabilizers, chelators) and baseline control buffer
Device-shear simulation rigs or representative nasal spray devices with characterized shear profiles
Immuno-capture reagents for canonical EV surface markers (anti-CD63/anti-CD9/anti-CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5) and capture-compatibility buffer panels
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS) and reagents
Density-fractionation materials (iodixanol) or SEC fractionation setup and fraction collectors
Protease (proteinase K), RNase reagents and detergent (e.g., Triton X-100) for membrane-disruption controls
Reagents and platforms for protected-cargo profiling (targeted small-RNA panel and targeted proteomics) with spike-in controls
Total protein assay reagents and consumables
secondary_readouts: Presence/absence and conservation of protected-cargo fingerprint (protected miRNAs and detergent/protease-sensitive proteins) across conditions and lots
Capture-compatibility metrics indicating assay interference vs true signal loss
experiment.success_criterion: Across >=3 independent lots, at least one orthogonal attribute (e.g., capture co-localization + detergent/protease sensitivity, or protected-cargo fingerprint) is reproducibly preserved under a defined set of storage/formulation/device conditions and reproducibly lost or substantially altered under at least one clinically relevant failure condition (e.g., specific excipient class or >=3 freeze-thaw cycles); capture-compatibility controls confirm that observed signal loss is not assay interference.

explicit_inferences: Preservation or loss of orthogonal intact-EV signatures will be more informative than bulk particle counts for detecting damaging storage/formulation conditions.
Assay controls (spike-in, capture-compatibility) are required to distinguish true biomaterial changes from assay interference.
falsification_criteria: No reproducible qualitative change in orthogonal intact-EV signatures across tested stability/formulation conditions and independent lots (n >= 3), or observed changes are attributable to assay interference per capture-compatibility and spike-in controls.
human_decisions_required: Select the protected-cargo targeted panels (miRNA + proteins) to include in protected-cargo readouts
Decide candidate formulation excipient matrix and device-shear envelope to test
Approve use of exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer and its identity
manufacturability_assessment: Feasible as an early orthogonal analytical program: requires access to fractionation (SEC/iodixanol), particle counting (NTA/TRPS), immuno-capture reagents, and targeted protected-cargo assays; no numeric release limits proposed at this exploratory stage.
manufacturing_rationale: Without stability-indicating attributes, lot-to-lot and process-scale differences may be masked by bulk particle counts; orthogonal, qualitative gates will guide permissible storage, handling, and formulation envelopes and de-risk Stage-1 scale-up and bridging activities (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).
measurement_strategy: Matrixed orthogonal assay panel across conditions with capture-compatibility and exogenous intact-EV spike-in controls; qualitative pass/fail calls per attribute per lot (non-numeric).
novelty_statement: This hypothesis is novel for SGL-001 because it explicitly proposes using a multi-layer orthogonal intact-EV analytical panel (capture co-localization with particle peaks, detergent/protease-protected cargo profiling, and particle:protein context) as qualitative stability-indicating attributes to gate formulation, storage, and comparability decisions. Prior SGL-001 work proposed identity and fractionation assays or in vivo bridging experiments, but did not package a stability-focused, spike-in–controlled orthogonal attribute panel as the primary output for shelf-life and formulation gating (differs from prior hypotheses that focused on fractionation, source-cell senescence, TFF envelope, or in vivo bridges).
principal_risks: Assay interference by formulation excipients could confound qualitative calls.
Insufficient material yield or assay sensitivity could prevent reproducible cross-lot conclusions.
Even if attributes are stability-indicating in vitro, in vivo delivery limitations (species/route) may still preclude translatability.
proposed_potency_relationship: Not claimed. Stability attributes are intended as identity/stability gates to preserve potential intact-EV-associated potency for downstream linkage experiments.
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: Adopt one or more orthogonal intact-EV-associated stability-indicating attributes (e.g., preservation of capture-positive particle-peak co-localization with detergent/protease-sensitive signal; presence of a protected-cargo fingerprint; stable protein:particle ratio) as qualitative acceptance gates for shelf-life, formulation suitability, and comparability decisions (non-numeric, pass/fail style).
title: Hypothesis: Orthogonal intact-EV identity and protected-cargo signals are stability-indicating for SGL-001
